\chapter{Como Se Dice --- The Sentence That Unlocks the Rest}
\label{ch:como-se-dice}
\hlchaptermodality{179}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can ask how something is said, and say which se that is.}

Complete ES-C52-como-se-dice: ask the question politely and say why it is impersonal rather than aimed at the listener.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[¿cómo se dice?]{¿cómo se dice? — the sentence that unlocks the rest}

\label{lesson:ES-C52-como-se-dice}



\begin{quote}
You know \emph{cómo}. You know the impersonal \emph{se}. Put them in front of \emph{dice} and you have the sentence that will teach you more Spanish than this book will.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{The two words}
\begin{quote}
\emph{\textbf{¿Cómo se dice?}} — How do you say it? / How is it said?
\end{quote}

Take it apart with what this chapter gave you. \emph{Se dice} is the impersonal: it asks how a thing \textbf{gets said}, without asking who says it. Not \emph{how do \textbf{you} say it}, though that is the natural English — Spanish is not pointing at the person you are talking to. It is asking about the language itself.

Which is exactly right, because you are not asking for their personal opinion. You are asking what the word is.

\begin{quote}
\emph{¿Cómo se dice \textquotedblleft{}book\textquotedblright{} en español?} — How do you say \textquotedblleft{}book\textquotedblright{} in Spanish? \emph{¿Cómo se dice, por favor?}
\end{quote}

\textbf{This is the most valuable sentence in the book}, and it is worth saying why. Every other sentence you have learned lets you say something you already know. This one gets you the thing you \textbf{do not} know, from the person in front of you, mid-conversation. A learner with this sentence and some patience out-learns one with twice the vocabulary and no way to ask.

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}¿Cómo se dice?\textquotedblright{} until it is one word
  \item \textquotedblleft{}¿Cómo se dice en español, por favor?\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:} This is the one to over-practise.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Ask how something is said. (\emph{\textbf{¿Cómo se dice?}}) Which \emph{se} is that? (The \textbf{impersonal} one — asking about the language, not the person.) Next: the three \emph{se}s, side by side, for the first time.
\end{tcolorbox}
